properties.name_en: Vake Park - Turtle Lake cable car
properties.name_ru: Канатная дорога Парк Ваке — озеро Туртл (Кус Тба)
properties.note: gondolas first appeared in 1965 (Georgia Travel); civil.ge in Nov 2010 called it the last Tbilisi cable car and said it had 'ceased running a couple of years ago' (so about 2008, the exact year is not established); modernised 2016 (gondolaproject); works today (Georgia Travel)

properties.name_en: University-Bagebi cable car
properties.note: built 1982 (OpenStreetMap) or 1983 (Wikidata/Commons, gondolaproject); stopped 'sometime in the 90s' (gondolaproject) - the exact year is NOT established, 1995 is a placeholder; rehabilitated, the city mayor announced the start of service for 20 April 2021 (Georgia Today, 25 Mar 2021: a plan, the actual opening day was not confirmed); works today (Georgia Travel, Madloba)

properties.name_en: Nutsubidze-Lisi Lake cable car
properties.note: WEAK DATES: 1978-1995 is only from a railway-enthusiast forum list (seen in a search snippet, the page itself was not readable); a 2025 ICOMOS poster says 'a 1980s line, decommissioned in the late 1990s'. Schematic straight line between the two former stations (OpenStreetMap ways 633414853 on Nutsubidze Street and 742183462, the former upper station near Lisi Lake)
built in the 1840s on the order of viceroy Vorontsov (Golovinsky prospekt); named Rustaveli in 1918; renovation and closure to traffic 2024-2026 (en Wikipedia)

properties.name_ru: Конка (конный трамвай), линия по Михайловскому проспекту
properties.note: SCHEMATIC. ru.wikipedia: the first konka line (1883) ran along Mikhailovsky (today David Aghmashenebeli) Avenue between Vorontsov Square and the railway station and was soon extended to Erivan (Freedom) Square (year not stated); the konka ceased in 1910 (gauge 914 mm). Opening date: ru.wikipedia 10 March 1883, en.wikipedia 3 April 1883. The line is drawn on the whole avenue as mapped today, so the real ends differ; the Freedom Square extension and the 1904 line on Kirochnaya (Marjanishvili) Street are not drawn. Electric tram lines (from 25 December 1904 to 4 December 2006) are not drawn: no open source gives their streets.

properties.note: SCHEMATIC. ru.wikipedia: the first konka line (1883) ran along Mikhailovsky (today David Aghmashenebeli) Avenue between Vorontsov Square and the railway station and was soon extended to Erivan (Freedom) Square (year not stated); the konka ceased in 1910 (gauge 914 mm). Opening date: ru.wikipedia 10 March 1883, en.wikipedia 3 April 1883. The line is drawn on the whole avenue as mapped today, so the real ends differ; the Freedom Square extension and the 1904 line on Kirochnaya (Marjanishvili) Street are not drawn. Electric tram lines (from 25 December 1904 to 4 December 2006) are not drawn: no open source gives their streets.

properties.name_en: Tram street (routes of the ka.wikipedia lists)

Years: the route lists of 1962 and 1986 (ka.wikipedia) and the lists of routes of 2000 (8 routes), 2003 (4 routes), 2005 (route 12) and the closing on 4 December 2006 (ru.wikipedia): between the lists the state is not known. properties.name_en: Tram line on the plan of 1913
properties.note: DRAWN ON THE 1913 PLAN (legend: 'line of the tram'). The points were read from the plan by an AI (Gemini) and snapped to the printed red line by a program, then checked by eye; the line can deviate by tens of metres and some stretches (for example in Avlabari and along the river) are uncertain. Streets as printed on the plan: Военно-Грузинская дорога (Дидубе); Муштаидскій проспектъ; Михайловскій проспектъ. Years: the plan is of 1913; the lines are shown while the plan is shown (1913-1922).

properties.name_en: Metekhi Bridge
properties.note: the Metekhi and Avlabari bridges were built side by side in 1805, rebuilt in 1821, 1843, 1870; in 1950-1951 both were replaced by the present single reinforced-concrete bridge (the crossing is older, the infobox says 8th century)
